ai.title: Refactor system prompts for strict tool formatting
ai.summary: Updated `main-prompt.ts` and `tools.ts` to enforce strict XML tool formatting, explicitly banning Markdown wrappers and mandating empty lines around tool calls. The `agent-instructions.md` file introduces a 'Buffy' persona with specific tone guidelines and clarifies state management rules. These changes aim to prevent parsing failures caused by improper tool call syntax.

eli5.text: Starting today, the coding assistant (Buffy) must format its tool calls using a strict XML-like structure, avoiding Markdown code fences and keeping blank lines around each call so the system can reliably parse them. A new persona named Buffy and updated tone guidelines now govern how the assistant responds, requiring enthusiastic phrases and proactive behavior. Developers working with the backend may notice that tool calls no longer render as formatted code blocks and that Buffy's messages consistently use an energetic tone, reflecting the new persona. These changes are live now and affect interactions with the assistant across supported platforms.

ai.title: Preserve partial content in LLM stream fallbacks
ai.summary: Stream fallback logic in `backend/src/llm-apis/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` now appends partially generated content to the message history before attempting the next provider. Previous implementations discarded mid-stream failures, causing context loss during rate limits or upstream errors. The change applies to Gemini 2.5 Pro (exp/preview) and OpenRouter streams, ensuring Claude Sonnet final fallback receives the full accumulated context.

eli5.text: When the assistant is generating a long response in real time and the service it's using suddenly stops working (for example, because it hit a usage limit), the assistant used to throw away everything it had already written and start over with a backup service. Now, it saves the partially written response and hands that text along to the next service it tries, so the new service can continue from where the old one left off instead of repeating yourself or losing your train of thought. This only affects how the assistant behaves behind the scenes when it's streaming responses and switching to a fallback option.

ai.title: OpenRouter error logging fix
ai.summary: OpenRouter stream error logging now passes raw error object to logger.error instead of extracting message. Replaces 'Error calling OpenAI API' with 'Error calling OpenRouter API Stream'. Adds console.log debug statement. Affects backend/src/llm-apis/open-router.ts.

eli5.text: When a streaming call to the AI fails, the system now logs the full error details and a clearer message instead of just the error text. This helps technical staff see what actually went wrong without digging into code logs. No end-user experience changes; only the internal debugging output is affected.

ai.title: Enforce nested XML elements for tool parameters
ai.summary: System prompts and tool instructions now mandate nested XML elements for parameters, explicitly forbidding XML attributes. This prevents parser errors caused by malformed tool calls. Changes apply to backend/src/main-prompt.ts, backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md, and backend/src/tools.ts. Examples updated to highlight correct nested structure.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions now require tool parameters to be written as nested XML elements instead of XML attributes. This means the assistant must use <parameter_name>value</parameter_name> format rather than <tool_name attribute="value">, preventing parsing errors. This change is live today and affects how the assistant generates tool calls internally.

eli5.text: You don't notice anything directly from this update, it just marks a new batch of fixes and improvements as ready to install. Behind the scenes, the software's version label was bumped so that people who install it get the latest mix of small changes, including better handling when an AI model drops part of a streamed response, a tweak to how errors from one of the model providers are recorded, an updated help link inside the app, and stricter formatting rules for how the assistant reads your instructions. Those changes were all made today and are now bundled into this release.

ai.title: writefile tool description drops XML attribute example
ai.summary: Removed the literal `<write_file path="foo">` negative example from the `write_file` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts`. The warning against XML attributes remains, now stated without the code snippet. Scope limited to the backend tool definition. This reduces prompt token usage and avoids potential parsing confusion from embedded XML tags in the instructions.

eli5.text: The assistant was given a shorter, clearer way to warn against a common formatting mistake: it used to show an example of the wrong way to format a request, and now it just says in plain text that the wrong format won't work. If you looked at the instructions the assistant follows, you'd see the example line is gone, replaced by a simpler sentence. Nothing about how the assistant actually writes files has changed; only the wording in its internal guidebook was trimmed down.

ai.title: Update readfile tool call response format to nested XML
ai.summary: read_file tool responses now use nested XML structure with separate <path> and <content> tags instead of attribute-based format. This change improves parsing reliability for file contents containing special characters or newlines. The update affects backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts renderReadFilesResult and parseReadFilesResult functions. Regex pattern updated to match new structure; path values now trimmed during parsing.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to read a file, it now wraps each file's address and contents in their own labeled sections instead of tucking everything into one tag. This makes it easier for the assistant to correctly pull out files that contain unusual characters or line breaks. You will not see any difference in your files or experience, but the behind-the-scenes reading process is now more reliable. The change is already in place and affects only the internal handling of file-reading requests.

ai.title: Catch XML parsing errors in backend tool calls
ai.summary: Added error handling for `parseRawToolCall` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to catch malformed XML tool calls before execution. Invalid calls now return a structured error result to the client instead of crashing the agent loop. Also cleaned up debug logging in `backend/src/llm-apis/open-router.ts` and improved error messaging in `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: If the assistant tries to use a tool with a command that is malformed, say, because letters are missing or it is badly structured, the app used to freeze or stop working entirely. Now, instead of crashing, it quietly flags the bad command, tells the user what went wrong, and keeps running so the assistant can try again. The helpful messages you see when something fails are also a bit clearer, and unnecessary debug text that was being printed by mistake has been removed. The change went live today.
